The '''1958 California Vulcans football team''' was an [[American football]] team that represented the California  State Teachers College (now known as [[California University of Pennsylvania]]) of [[California, Pennsylvania]], as a member of the [[Pennsylvania State Athletic Conference|Pennsylvania State Teachers College Conference]] (PSTCC) during the [[1958 college football season]]. In their ninth year under head coach [[Ted Nemeth]], the Vulcans compiled a perfect 8–0 record (6–0 against PSTCC opponents), won the PSTCC championship, and outscored opponents by a total of 202 to 31.<ref>{{cite web|title=California Yearly Results|publisher=[[College Football Data Warehouse]]|accessdate=May 5, 2023|url=http://www.cfbdatawarehouse.com/data/active/c/california_pa/1955-1959_yearly_results.php|archive-date=September 6, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906145101/http://www.cfbdatawarehouse.com/data/active/c/california_pa/1955-1959_yearly_results.php|url-status=dead}}</ref>

California and West Chester both compiled undefeated records against conference opponents, but California was declared the conference champion under the "Saylor-system" used by the PSTCC which took into account overall win-loss record and caliber of opposition.<ref>{{cite news|title=Western Team Finally Captures STC Crown|newspaper=The Daily Record|location=East Stroudsburg, Pennsylvania|date=November 18, 1958|page=8|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-pocono-record-western-team-finally-c/124086699/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref> It was the first time a team from western Pennsylvania won the PSTCC championship.<ref>{{cite news|title=Tech's Amazing Win District's Highlight: California Teachers' Victory Gives Them Conference Title, Bowl Shot|newspaper=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|date=November 17, 1958|page=26|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/pittsburgh-post-gazette-techs-amazing-w/124086808/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>

California's senior left halfback Carl Trimber was the leading scorer in the PSTCC. The Vulcans also had the best scoring defense in the conference, giving up only 31 points in eight games. Against the rush, the Vulcans allowed an average of only 42 yards per game.<ref name=DR>{{cite news|title=California Vulcans Are Tops In Offense, Defense: Combination Meant Perfect Mark For CSTC|newspaper=The Daily Republican|date=November 20, 1958|page=3|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daily-republican-california-vulcans/124086989/|via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}</ref>
